title: Logic Restructuring with Preserved Logic Blocks
problem: Technology-independent logic optimization over-decomposes complex cells (adders, multiplexers) that should be preserved for technology mapping, degrading final PPA results.
motivation: Complex cells in standard cell libraries can significantly improve timing, area, and power, but traditional optimization decomposes them into gates, preventing effective use during technology mapping.
method: Proposes 'boxing' logic blocks before optimization and preserving them during resubstitution. Transparent-boxing leverages information about boxed logic for better optimization than black-boxing, using wire-based resubstitution to optimize boxed networks while maintaining structure.
key_novelty: Transparent-boxing approach that preserves complex-cell structures while still utilizing their internal logic for cross-block optimization.
contributions: 4% additional mapped network size reduction vs. black-boxing
1.8% timing improvement over black-boxing across full design flow
Maintains similar improvements in area, power, and wire length

metrics.other: 4% mapped size reduction, 1.8% timing improvement, area/power/wirelength parity

limitations: Not discussed; evaluation focuses on academic and industrial benchmarks but scalability to very large designs unclear.
primary_theme: Logic optimization preserving complex cell structures
